description:
Episode 9 of a daily journey through the universe. 🛰️
We catch up with Voyager 1: launched in 1977, now one full light-day from Earth (a milestone reached on Nov 18, 2026), a golden record for aliens, and the Pale Blue Dot.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 10: Next stop, our nearest star. And how long it would really take to get there.

Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

segments.text: Episode nine. Next stop... Voyager one.
Launched in nineteen seventy-seven, Voyager one is the farthest object humans have ever made.
segments.headline: Launched in 1977

segments.text: It's now about twenty-six billion kilometers away, and still moving.
So far that its radio signals take a full day to reach us. This week, it became the first human-made object ever to get that far.

visual.label: for its signal to reach Earth

segments.text: In twenty twelve, it became the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space, leaving the Sun's bubble behind.
segments.headline: Now in interstellar space

segments.text: On board is a golden record, with music, sounds of Earth, and greetings in fifty-five languages. A message for anyone who finds it.
segments.headline: A message for aliens

segments.text: And in nineteen ninety, it turned around and took a photo of home. Earth, as a single pale blue dot.
segments.headline: The Pale Blue Dot

segments.text: Tomorrow, we leave the solar system. Next stop: our nearest star, and how long it would really take to get there. Follow, so you don't miss episode ten.
